title: Working at Redwood — roles, career ladders, benefits, onboarding, and internal tools (2026 Q1)
author: Emma Nguyen
body:
Overview

This page is Redwood's canonical employee handbook summary: a single-page reference covering how we work, role structure and career ladders, core benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding expectations, and the internal tools new hires will use. Use the left navigation to reach deeper, role-specific, and team-specific pages.

Principles and culture

- Developer-first, product-minded: we prioritize engineering quality and customer impact.
- Ownership and clarity: clear ownership for services and processes, documented runbooks, and reliable handoffs.
- Inclusive growth: career ladders and calibration processes support transparent development.

1. Roles & career ladders

Summary
- Redwood organizes seniority with leveled ladders for Engineering, Product, Design, Sales, Customer Success, and People Ops. Ladders are competency-based and calibrated annually during promotion cycles.

Engineering ladder (high level)
- E1: New grad / individual contributor, learning core systems and codebase.
- E2: Solid contributor, owns feature work and small projects.
- E3: Senior IC, owns cross-team features, mentors others.
- E4: Staff Engineer, leads architecture and technical strategy for major subsystems.
- E5: Principal / Distinguished Engineer, company-wide technical leadership and long-term roadmap.

Promotion process (summary)
1. Candidate prepares promotion packet (self-assessment, 3–5 peer feedback notes, impact examples).
2. Manager reviews and submits to calibration board.
3. Calibration board reviews against rubric and either approves, requests more evidence, or defers.
4. HR notifies outcome and coordinates compensation changes.

Career development resources
- Quarterly career conversations (1:1 agenda template linked).
- Mentorship program (apply via People Ops).
- Learning stipend and role-based training tracks.

2. Hiring & onboarding overview

Hiring philosophy
- We hire for craft, ownership, and mission alignment. Interview loops balance technical craft and product judgment with role-specific skills.
- Diversity and inclusion: interview panels must include at least one panelist trained in inclusive hiring and one interviewer from outside the immediate team when possible.

Standard interview loop (Engineering)
1. Recruiter screen (30 min) — role fit and logistics.
2. Technical screen (45–60 min) — coding + problem solving.
3. Take-home or take-home design exercise (where required).
4. Onsite loop (4–6 interviews) — system design, coding, behavioral, and team fit.
5. Hiring manager debrief and decision.

Offer & acceptance
- Offers include salary, equity, start date, and an outline of benefits. People Ops owns offer letters and immigration support for international hires.

Onboarding timeline (30/60/90)
- Day 0–1: Account provisioning, access to docs, and welcome with manager.
- Week 1: Team onboarding, product overview, first small task.
- Month 1: Deliver first visible contribution and complete required security and compliance training.
- Month 3: Alignment review with manager to validate performance expectations and growth plan.

Onboarding owners and runbooks
- Manager: role expectations, initial 1:1 cadence, first-90 plan.
- Buddy: peer to answer day-to-day product and culture questions (assigned during offer acceptance).
- People Ops: benefits enrollment, payroll, equity paperwork, and compliance training.

3. Benefits & perks

Summary (high level)
- Competitive base salary + equity, medical/dental/vision coverage, parental leave, flexible PTO, and commuter/remote stipends (where applicable).

Health and wellness
- Medical: multiple plan options with employer contribution.
- Mental health: employee assistance program (EAP) and covered therapy sessions.

Family & leave
- Parental leave: primary caregiver 18 weeks paid, secondary caregiver 8 weeks paid (policy subject to local law).
- Caregiver leave and paid time for new parent transition coaching.

Financial and retirement
- 401(k) (or local equivalent) with company match where available.
- Annual performance bonus and equity refresh programs for tenured employees.

Time off and flexible work
- Flexible PTO policy with manager alignment for planned absences.
- Paid company holidays + discretionary off days (Winter focus days).
- Work-from-home stipends and equipment allowance for remote-first employees.

Learning and development
- Annual learning stipend ($1,200 USD) for conferences, courses, or books.
- Internal lunch-and-learn series and technical brown-bags.

Perks and regional variations
- Commuter benefits, co-working allowances for certain markets, and wellbeing credits vary by region — consult People Ops for country-specific details.

4. Internal tools & access

Core systems new hires will use
- Single sign-on (SSO): Okta for identity and app access.
- Docs & collaboration: Confluence (policy + handbook), Google Workspace (email, drive), Slack (team communication).
- Code & CI: GitHub (repos + PRs), CircleCI/Argo (pipelines), internal CI dashboards.
- Service and infra: Terraform repo, AWS console (least-privilege roles), Datadog (metrics and tracing), Sentry (errors).
- Customer & support tools: Zendesk/Intercom (region-dependent), Gainsight for enterprise customers.

Access process and timing
- New-hire provisioning is triggered on Day 0 after background check completes. Typical access timeline:
  - Okta + Google: Day 0–1
  - GitHub + CI access: Day 1–3
  - AWS least-privilege role & project access: Day 2–7 (requires manager approval)

Example CLI snippet (for internal dev environment access)

- To fetch development secrets (developers only):

  ```bash
  # Authenticate via Okta CLI first
  okta login --org redwood-inference
  export AWS_PROFILE=redwood-dev
  aws ssm get-parameter --name "/redwood/dev/stripe/api_key" --with-decryption --region us-west-2
  ```

Security and compliance requirements
- All hires must complete Security Awareness and Data Handling training within the first 14 days.
- MFA is mandatory for all accounts.
- For roles that handle customer data we enforce additional controls (approved devices, full-disk encryption, and role-specific access reviews).

5. Day 1 checklist for new hires (concise)

- Pre-Day 1: signed offer, background check cleared, buddy assigned, hardware shipped.
- Day 0–1 checklist:
  1. Complete Okta and Google sign-in and set MFA.
  2. Read the Welcome packet and team README in Confluence.
  3. Join relevant Slack channels (#all, #eng, #team-<name>, #random).
  4. Complete security and data-handling training.
  5. Verify GitHub access and open your first onboarding PR (example: update your README).

6. Manager responsibilities and review cadence

Manager runbook (first 30 days)
1. Schedule recurring 1:1s (weekly for the first 3 months, then biweekly).
2. Set clear 30/60/90 expectations and confirm first deliverable.
3. Conduct weekly check-ins with buddy to identify blocker patterns.
4. Complete initial onboarding survey at Day 14 and 30.

Performance reviews and calibration
- Formal review cycles occur twice per year (June and December).
- Promotion windows align with reviews, but off-cycle promotion exceptions exist for extraordinary impact.

7. FAQs and troubleshooting

Q: How do I request additional hardware?
A: Submit a ticket to IT via the Helpdesk (link in Confluence) and copy your manager for expedited approval.

Q: Who do I contact for payroll or equity questions?
A: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.ai) handles payroll, equity grants, and country-specific benefits.

Q: Where are role-specific comp band details stored?
A: Compensation bands are maintained in the HR portal (People Ops will provide access on Day 1 after orientation).
